title: Top-dimensional flatness decomposes by generic free rank
statement: Let $S,X$ be affine schemes [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-affine-spectrum], let $g:X\to S$ be smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] with geometrically irreducible nonempty fibres [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], and let $E$ be a finitely presented quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation]. For a scheme $T\to S$ put $X_T=X\times_ST$ and let $E_T$ be tensor pullback [def-pc-fibre-product], [def-pc-module-pullback]. For $r\geq0$ define $H_r(T)$ to be a singleton if, for every $t\in T$, $E_T$ is free of rank $r$ on an open neighbourhood in $X_T$ of the unique generic point $\xi_t$ of $(X_T)_t$, and empty otherwise. Free of rank $r$ means isomorphic to $\mathcal O_{X_T}^{\oplus r}$ on that neighbourhood. A generic point is a point whose closure is the whole fibre [def-sc-generic-point]. Assume additionally that $g$ has constant relative dimension $a\geq0$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Define $F_a(T)$ to be a singleton if $(E_T)_x$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{T,t}$ for every $x\in X_T$ with image $t$ such that $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(t)}\kappa(x)\geq a$, and empty otherwise [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over], [def-weil-residue-field], [def-kun-transcendence-degree]. There is an integer $c\geq0$ such that $H_r$ is empty for $r>c$ and $F_a\simeq\coprod_{r=0}^c H_r$ as sheaves on $S$-schemes for the Zariski topology. Explicitly, $F_a(T)$ is nonempty if and only if there is a decomposition into pairwise disjoint open and closed subschemes $T=\coprod_{r=0}^c T_r$ such that $E_{T_r}$ is free of rank $r$ near every fibre generic point; whenever it exists this decomposition is unique. The coproduct is the sheaf coproduct: a disconnected test scheme may have different ranks on different components.

source.place: Tag 05UE (lemma-compare-H-F), including its finite generator bound and local freeness near the generic point; the coproduct is interpreted as the sheaf coproduct.

proof.text: Put $A=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ and $N=\Gamma(X,E)$. The affine finite-presentation result makes $N$ finitely presented, hence generated by $c\geq0$ elements. The affine tilde–sections counit identifies $E$ with $\widetilde N$, and tilde preserves cokernels. Thus a generating surjection $A^c\twoheadrightarrow N$ gives $\mathcal O_X^c\twoheadrightarrow E$. Pullback is a left adjoint, so it preserves this surjection and the finite free source. Tensoring its stalk at any $x\in X_T$ with $\kappa(x)$ gives a surjection $\kappa(x)^c\twoheadrightarrow(E_T)_x\otimes\kappa(x)$. Consequently every finite free rank occurring there is at most $c$. In particular $H_r(T)$ is empty for $r>c$ whenever $T$ is nonempty. At the empty test scheme it is a singleton, as required of the initial Zariski sheaf.

source.place: Tag 05UE (lemma-compare-H-F), first two sentences (uniform generator bound)

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary $T\to S$ and write $p:X_T\to T$. Smooth relative dimension $a$ survives this base change. Smoothness implies flatness and local finite presentation. Moreover $g$ is affine because $X,S$ are affine; it is therefore quasi-compact and separated. Thus $g$, and then $p$, are of finite presentation. These statements do not require $T$ affine or Noetherian. Each fibre $Y=(X_T)_t$ is affine and smooth over $\kappa(t)$; it is nonempty and irreducible by the geometric irreducibility hypothesis, and reduced by smoothness. In particular $Y$ is integral. Tensor pullback also preserves the finite presentation of $E$, so $E_T$ is finitely presented.

source.place: Tag 05UE (lemma-compare-H-F), third sentence and the hypotheses of its last-sentence input Tag 080Q

proof.text: For such a fibre write $Y=\operatorname{Spec}B$, with $B$ a finite type integral $\kappa(t)$-algebra. Its local topological dimension is $a$ everywhere by relative dimension. For a point $x$ corresponding to $\mathfrak q$, the dimension formula gives $a=\dim B_{\mathfrak q}+\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(t)}\kappa(x)$. The unique generic point corresponds to $(0)$; its local ring is a field by the reduced-minimal-prime lemma, so its transcendence degree is $a$. If $\mathfrak q\ne(0)$, the prime chain $(0)\subsetneq\mathfrak q$ survives in $B_{\mathfrak q}$, giving $\dim B_{\mathfrak q}\geq1$ and transcendence degree strictly less than $a$. Hence the points tested by $F_a(T)$ are exactly the fibre generic points $\xi_t$. In particular their fibre local rings are fields.

source.place: Tag 05UE (lemma-compare-H-F), flatness in dimensions at least d is flatness at the unique generic point

proof.text: Assume $F_a(T)$ is nonempty and fix $t\in T$. Step 3 gives base-flatness of $(E_T)_{\xi_t}$ over $\mathcal O_{T,t}$. The stalk of its fibre restriction is a module over the field $\mathcal O_{(X_T)_t,\xi_t}$, so it is flat (tensoring vector spaces over a field is exact). Apply the flat-and-fibre-flat criterion to $p:X_T\to T$ and $E_T$, whose finite-presentation hypotheses were checked in Step 2. It supplies an open neighbourhood $U$ of $\xi_t$ in $X_T$ and an integer $r\geq0$ with $E_T|_U\simeq\mathcal O_U^r$. Step 1 gives $r\leq c$, including the possible value $r=0$.

source.place: Tag 05UE (lemma-compare-H-F), last sentence: More on Morphisms Tag 080Q (lemma-flat-and-free-at-point-fibre)

proof.text: The image $V=p(U)$ is open in $T$, because $p$ is flat and locally of finite presentation and hence universally open. It contains $t$. If $v\in V$, then $U\cap(X_T)_v$ is a nonempty open of the irreducible fibre $(X_T)_v$, so it contains its generic point $\xi_v$. The same isomorphism on $U$ therefore witnesses rank $r$ on a neighbourhood of every $\xi_v$ for $v\in V$; after restriction to $X_V$ this says $H_r(V)\ne\varnothing$. This is the precise meaning of the source's sentence that $H_r$ contains the image of $U$: it asserts the condition on all fibres over $V$, without asserting that $E_T$ is free on all of $X_V$.

source.place: Tag 05UE (lemma-compare-H-F), penultimate sentence: the image of U is an open neighbourhood of t

proof.text: Conversely, if $H_r(V)$ is nonempty for an open subscheme $V\subseteq T$, then near each fibre generic point $E_V$ is finite free over the structure sheaf. The structure stalk is flat over $\mathcal O_{V,v}$ by smoothness of $p$, and a finite direct sum of copies of a flat module is flat: tensoring a finite direct sum is the direct sum of the exact tensor functors. Thus $(E_V)_{\xi_v}$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{V,v}$. Step 3 now gives $F_a(V)\ne\varnothing$. The same applies on any open cover of $T$, since the stalk conditions defining $F_a$ are local on $T$.

They identify the same finite-dimensional vector space with $\kappa(\xi_t)^r$ and $\kappa(\xi_t)^q$, forcing $r=q$. For $F_a(T)
e\varnothing$, let $T_r$ be the union of all open $V\subseteq T$ with $H_r(V)

proof.text: For completeness, use the existing generic-rank representability statement only for its assertion that the assignments $H_r$ are functors under tensor pullback. Their Zariski sheaf condition also follows directly: the existence of the specified free neighbourhood at each fibre generic point can be checked on an open cover of the base. Steps 5–7 show that $F_a$ is stable under arbitrary base change: pull back a witnessing open cover by $H_r$, use functoriality of $H_r$, and apply Step 6. Its restriction maps are therefore the unique maps of singleton-or-empty sets. Its Zariski sheaf condition is the locality of its defining stalk predicate. To verify the claimed coproduct, take any Zariski sheaf $G$ and maps $H_r\to G$. For the unique element of $F_a(T)$, restrict to the canonical clopen partition of Step 7, apply the map $H_r(T_r)\to G(T_r)$, and glue. Overlaps are empty, where every sheaf has exactly one section, so the sections are compatible. The partition pulls back to the unique rank partition on every base change, so this construction is natural. Its restrictions force uniqueness, and conversely every map $F_a\to G$ restricts to the given maps on $H_r$. This is precisely the universal property of the sheaf coproduct.

U : Fin (c + 1) → T.left.Opens, smoothGenericRankPartition g E c T U
